intro: Syria's people are mostly Arab, with Kurds, Armenians, Assyrians, Turkmen and others, and many religious communities.

chapters.title: Peoples and faiths
text: Most Syrians are Sunni Muslim. There are Alawite, Druze, Ismaili and Christian communities, and Kurds live mainly in the north-east.
Arabic is the official language; Kurdish, Armenian and Aramaic are also spoken. Aramaic, the language of Jesus, survives in the village of Maaloula.

chapters.title: Displaced
text: Millions of Syrians live abroad as refugees, and many have begun returning since 2024.

keyTerms.meaning: An ancient language once spoken across the Middle East.
